findings.summary: 3D Systems Corporation is an American public company that engineers and sells 3D printing materials and application engineering services. Founded in 1986 by Chuck Hull, inventor of stereolithography, the company is headquartered in Rock Hill, South Carolina. It manufactures a range of additive manufacturing systems including stereolithography (SLA), fused deposition modeling (FDM), selective laser sintering (SLS), color-jet printing, multi-jet printing, and direct metal printing. These systems convert digital 3D data into physical objects through additive layer-by-layer processes. The company serves worldwide markets with products spanning desktop printers to industrial metal printing systems, and offers related services such as CNC machining, injection molding, and medical-grade prototyping.

mechanisms.title: Additive Layer Fabrication
mechanisms.explanation: Systems convert digital 3D data into physical objects through an additive layer-by-layer process. Each technology deposits or solidifies material in successive layers to build a part from the bottom up.

mechanisms.title: Material-Specific Process Variation
mechanisms.explanation: Different technologies use distinct material handling: stereolithography uses photopolymer resin cured by light; fused deposition modeling extrudes thermoplastic filament; selective laser sintering fuses powdered material with a laser; color-jet printing binds powder with liquid binder; direct metal printing uses metal powder sintering. Systems vary in materials, print capacities, and applications.
